	</div><p>ISLAMABAD: Security forces have killed seven Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district, security sources said on Friday.</p><p>The IBO was carried out against India-backed militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, with several hideouts also destroyed, they said.</p><p>Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the militants during the operation, the security sources said.</p><p>Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif lauded the security forces for killing seven terrorists in North Waziristan.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">
			<div class="embed_external_url tweetPost" id="2108445542271623229" style="width: 100%;height: 100%;"><div class="twitter-tweet twitter-tweet-rendered" style="display: flex; max-width: 550px; width: 100%; margin-top: 10px; margin-bottom: 10px;"></div></div>
		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>The latest operation comes a day after forces killed nine Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation carried out in several areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district, security sources said.</p><p>The IBOs were conducted in Palangzai, Nadeem Kot and Kot Khazri areas of North Waziristan, said the security sources.</p><p>Pakistan has witnessed a sharp rise in cross-border terrorist incidents, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in 2021.</p><p>Pakistan recorded its highest monthly number of militant attacks in 12 years during September 2026.</p><p>According to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring anti-state violence in the region, 225 militant attacks were recorded across the country in September, compared with 199 in August — an increase of 13%. Militant attacks increased for the third consecutive month.</p><p>Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent its territory from being used by militant organisations to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.</p><p>Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban authorities have failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.</p><p>Despite multiple rounds of talks, Islamabad and Kabul have yet to resolve their differences, with the issue of militant groups operating from Afghan soil remaining a major point of contention between the two sides.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: Security forces neutralise seven India-backed terrorists in North Waziristan IBO: sources
subheadline: Weapons and ammunition recovered from Fitna al-Khawarij terrorists during operation, say security sources
author: Zarmeen Zehra
article_text:
IBO carried out against terrorists under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision.
Operation carried out in North Waziristan district: security sources.
PM Shehbaz lauds security forces for killing nine terrorists.

ISLAMABAD: Security forces have killed seven Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation (IBO) in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district, security sources said on Friday.

The IBO was carried out against India-backed militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under the Azm-e-Istehkam vision, with several hideouts also destroyed, they said.

Weapons and ammunition were recovered from the militants during the operation, the security sources said.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif lauded the security forces for killing seven terrorists in North Waziristan.

The latest operation comes a day after forces killed nine Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists during an intelligence-based operation carried out in several areas of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district, security sources said.

The IBOs were conducted in Palangzai, Nadeem Kot and Kot Khazri areas of North Waziristan, said the security sources.

Pakistan has witnessed a sharp rise in cross-border terrorist incidents, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the Afghan Taliban returned to power in 2021.

Pakistan recorded its highest monthly number of militant attacks in 12 years during September 2026.

According to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), an Islamabad-based independent think tank monitoring anti-state violence in the region, 225 militant attacks were recorded across the country in September, compared with 199 in August — an increase of 13%. Militant attacks increased for the third consecutive month.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged Kabul to prevent its territory from being used by militant organisations to carry out attacks inside Pakistan.

Pakistan maintains that the Afghan Taliban authorities have failed to take effective action against groups responsible for attacks on Pakistani security forces and civilians.

Despite multiple rounds of talks, Islamabad and Kabul have yet to resolve their differences, with the issue of militant groups operating from Afghan soil remaining a major point of contention between the two sides.

                        <h2>Various parts of Balochistan are expected to receive rain under the influence of westerly weather system</h2>

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="" spellcheck="false">A volunteer sprays water on a passer-by to cool him off at a roadside camp in the metropolis amid scorching heat.— Online </figcaption><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><superhuman-go-underlines data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; display: contents; --rem: 16;"></superhuman-go-underlines></figure></div><p>The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast hotter weather conditions in Karachi, with maximum temperatures likely to range between 36°C and 38°C from Monday.</p><p>The Met Office said changing atmospheric conditions could affect the intensity of sea breezes, potentially influencing weather conditions in the port city.</p><style>

	</div><p>Although temperatures are expected to rise, the mercury is likely to remain within the normal range for the month of October, it said.</p><p>According to the PMD, Karachi is experiencing partly cloudy weather today, with southwesterly winds blowing at a speed of 10 to 20 kilometres per hour.</p><p>Meanwhile, a new westerly weather system is expected to affect the country's upper and northern regions from October 12, the department said.</p><p>Under the influence of this system, rain is also possible in various parts of Balochistan.</p>                    </div>

headline: PMD forecasts hot weather conditions in Karachi from Monday
subheadline: Various parts of Balochistan are expected to receive rain under the influence of westerly weather system
author: Uneeba Zameer Shah
article_text:
The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) has forecast hotter weather conditions in Karachi, with maximum temperatures likely to range between 36°C and 38°C from Monday.

The Met Office said changing atmospheric conditions could affect the intensity of sea breezes, potentially influencing weather conditions in the port city.

Although temperatures are expected to rise, the mercury is likely to remain within the normal range for the month of October, it said.

According to the PMD, Karachi is experiencing partly cloudy weather today, with southwesterly winds blowing at a speed of 10 to 20 kilometres per hour.

Meanwhile, a new westerly weather system is expected to affect the country's upper and northern regions from October 12, the department said.

Under the influence of this system, rain is also possible in various parts of Balochistan.

	</div><p>Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistan remains committed to a negotiated and peaceful outcome to the Middle East conflict and does not want it to widen further.</p><p>“We want that this conflict should not expand horizontally or vertically,” the chief military spokesperson said in an interview with <span style="font-style: italic;">CNN,</span> adding that Pakistan was doing and would continue to do whatever was possible and necessary to narrow differences and gaps between the parties.</p><p>Asked whether Pakistan could remain a neutral broker given Iran’s attacks on Saudi Arabia and the involvement of the Iran-aligned Houthis, Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan had demonstrated that it was an “honest broker”.</p><p>“I think what Pakistan has been doing is exhibiting that we have been a very honest broker,” he said, adding that neutrality stemmed from honesty and that Pakistan had been clear about its position with all its partners and friends.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

<p>The ISPR DG further said Pakistan had openly condemned attacks on Iran by Israel and the United States. He added that Pakistan had also openly condemned Iran’s attacks on Arab and Gulf countries.</p><p>“We do not mince our words. Why? Because we have a stake in regional peace and stability,” he said.</p><p>“We tell all that nobody benefits from expanding this war,” the ISPR chief added.</p><p>While replying to a question on the Makkah pact, the ISPR DG said: "Pakistan is delving into the operationalisation of forces, adding that the Makkah Accord will be purely defensive and its implementation will be determined by operational commanders amid numerous security challenges and emerging threats in the region."</p><p>Asked by <span style="font-style: italic;">CNN </span>whether Pakistani troops or personnel were already on the ground in Saudi Arabia as part of the Makkah alliance, the ISPR DG said the forces had been there for decades.</p><p>“Pakistani troops have been there for decades […] in Saudi Arabia,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said.</p><p>He said the Makkah alliance had not emerged “in a vacuum”, pointing to the longstanding diplomatic, political, military and people-to-people ties between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.</p><p>“So I can share with you that Pakistani troops, in multiple capabilities and domains, are already there,” the ISPR DG said.</p><p>The remarks come after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye agreed to immediately implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the “rapid deployment” of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.</p><p>The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh on Monday, according to a joint statement shared by Pakistan’s Foreign Office.</p><p>The three countries said the deployment would take place under approved arrangements and in accordance with their respective national laws, with the measures aimed at enhancing readiness, military integration and collective capacity.</p><p>The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August. Under the agreement, an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: Mediator Pakistan doesn't want Mideast conflict to widen further: top military spox
subheadline: Lt Gen Chaudhry says Pakistani actions demonstrated that it is an “honest broker” in Middle East conflict
author: Web Desk
article_text:
Pakistan acts as "honest broker" in Middle East conflict: ISPR DG.
Makkah Accord will be purely defensive, says DG ISPR.
"Operational commanders to determine implementation of pact."

Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistan remains committed to a negotiated and peaceful outcome to the Middle East conflict and does not want it to widen further.

“We want that this conflict should not expand horizontally or vertically,” the chief military spokesperson said in an interview with CNN, adding that Pakistan was doing and would continue to do whatever was possible and necessary to narrow differences and gaps between the parties.

Asked whether Pakistan could remain a neutral broker given Iran’s attacks on Saudi Arabia and the involvement of the Iran-aligned Houthis, Lt Gen Chaudhry said Pakistan had demonstrated that it was an “honest broker”.

“I think what Pakistan has been doing is exhibiting that we have been a very honest broker,” he said, adding that neutrality stemmed from honesty and that Pakistan had been clear about its position with all its partners and friends.

The ISPR DG further said Pakistan had openly condemned attacks on Iran by Israel and the United States. He added that Pakistan had also openly condemned Iran’s attacks on Arab and Gulf countries.

“We do not mince our words. Why? Because we have a stake in regional peace and stability,” he said.

“We tell all that nobody benefits from expanding this war,” the ISPR chief added.

While replying to a question on the Makkah pact, the ISPR DG said: "Pakistan is delving into the operationalisation of forces, adding that the Makkah Accord will be purely defensive and its implementation will be determined by operational commanders amid numerous security challenges and emerging threats in the region."

Asked by CNN whether Pakistani troops or personnel were already on the ground in Saudi Arabia as part of the Makkah alliance, the ISPR DG said the forces had been there for decades.

“Pakistani troops have been there for decades […] in Saudi Arabia,” Lt Gen Chaudhry said.

He said the Makkah alliance had not emerged “in a vacuum”, pointing to the longstanding diplomatic, political, military and people-to-people ties between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

“So I can share with you that Pakistani troops, in multiple capabilities and domains, are already there,” the ISPR DG said.

The remarks come after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye agreed to immediately implement their collective defence commitments and ensure the “rapid deployment” of agreed military forces and capabilities in Saudi Arabia.

The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh on Monday, according to a joint statement shared by Pakistan’s Foreign Office.

The three countries said the deployment would take place under approved arrangements and in accordance with their respective national laws, with the measures aimed at enhancing readiness, military integration and collective capacity.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August. Under the agreement, an armed attack against one member is considered an attack against all.

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">A passenger aircraft descends to land at Heathrow Airport in London, Britain, January 5, 2022. — Reuters</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b>Airline suspends flights to Riyadh only.</b></li><li><b>PAA dismisses social media speculation.</b></li><li><b>Riyadh airport attacks prompt wider aviation concerns.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>KARACHI: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has temporarily suspended flights to Riyadh, the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) confirmed, clarifying that other flight operations to Saudi Arabia continue as usual.</p><p>“Flight operations to Saudi Arabia are continuing as usual. <p>The clarification comes amid heightened concerns following attacks on Riyadh airport on Thursday, which Saudi authorities said killed three people and injured several others.</p><p>The attacks damaged a Saudia Airlines aircraft and prompted several airlines to cancel flights to the Saudi capital.</p><p>Yemen’s Houthi group also repeated threats against aircraft flying over Saudi Arabia, except those operating above the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah.</p><p>Meanwhile, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency extended the area in which it advised airlines against flying, citing the recent attacks on Riyadh airport and risks to civil aviation.</p><p>The PAA did not provide further details about the duration of PIA’s suspension of flights to Riyadh.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: PIA temporarily suspends Riyadh flights, confirms PAA
subheadline: Pakistan Airports Authority says other flight operations to Saudi Arabia continue as usual
author: Tariq Abul Hasan
article_text:
Airline suspends flights to Riyadh only.
PAA dismisses social media speculation.
Riyadh airport attacks prompt wider aviation concerns.

KARACHI: Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) has temporarily suspended flights to Riyadh, the Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) confirmed, clarifying that other flight operations to Saudi Arabia continue as usual.

“Flight operations to Saudi Arabia are continuing as usual. PIA has temporarily suspended flights only to Riyadh,” the PAA said in a statement.

It also rejected speculation circulating on social media, saying such claims were “not true”.

The clarification comes amid heightened concerns following attacks on Riyadh airport on Thursday, which Saudi authorities said killed three people and injured several others.

The attacks damaged a Saudia Airlines aircraft and prompted several airlines to cancel flights to the Saudi capital.

Yemen’s Houthi group also repeated threats against aircraft flying over Saudi Arabia, except those operating above the holy cities of Makkah and Madinah.

Meanwhile, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency extended the area in which it advised airlines against flying, citing the recent attacks on Riyadh airport and risks to civil aviation.

The PAA did not provide further details about the duration of PIA’s suspension of flights to Riyadh.

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari addresses an event in Karachi on October 9, 2026. — YouTube/Geo News/screengrab </figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b>PPP chairman says PTI’s politics is harming the party.</b></li><li><b>High-level meeting expected to review security reports.</b></li><li><b>Emergency proposal covers 12 districts, including merged areas.<br></b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has urged the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to abandon “extremist” politics as sources said that the federal government was weighing imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.</p><p>The developments have come as PTI presses on with its long march towards Islamabad, demanding the release of its founder, Imran Khan.</p><style>

headline: Bilawal urges PTI to shun 'extremist' politics as govt 'weighs' KP emergency, governor's rule
subheadline: PTI pressing on with its march to Islamabad; high-level govt meeting takes place today, say sources
author: Waqar Satti, Web Desk
article_text:
PPP chairman says PTI’s politics is harming the party.
High-level meeting expected to review security reports.
Emergency proposal covers 12 districts, including merged areas.

ISLAMABAD: Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has urged the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) to abandon “extremist” politics as sources said that the federal government was weighing imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The developments have come as PTI presses on with its long march towards Islamabad, demanding the release of its founder, Imran Khan.

Bilawal, in a speech during an event in Karachi, said Pakistan’s political history showed that those in prison today could be in power tomorrow, but stressed that the PTI would have to give up what he described as extremist politics.

“History shows that those who are in prison today will not necessarily remain in prison tomorrow,” he said, warning that Khan could surpass President Asif Ali Zardari’s record of 14 years in prison if the party continued on its current political path.

Bilawal criticised Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, accusing him of pursuing negative politics. He said the PTI’s confrontational approach was ultimately harming the party itself.

The PPP chairman urged the PTI to abandon its current approach, return to parliamentary committees and engage in dialogue with the federal government, saying these steps could help improve the situation.

                        <div class="detail-heading">

                                <div class="heading_H"><h1>Makkah alliance: Pakistan reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia</h1></div>
                                    <div class="except" style="margin-bottom: 12px;">
                        <h2>Pakistani forces would not cross into Yemen to launch attacks against Houthi forces, says FO spokesperson</h2>
                    </div>
                                <div class="time-section"  >
                                            <div class="source">
                                                            <span class="by_author">By</span>



        <div class="author_title_img" style="color:#000">
                            <span class="author_agency">APP</span>
            </div>
                                <span class="author_seperator"> | </span>
                            <p class="post-date-time">
                              Published October 09, 2026                            </p>
                        </div>
                                        
                </div>
            </div>
            <div class="left">
                <div class="story-area">
                    <div class="content-area">
                        <div class="medium-insert-images ui-sortable"><figure contenteditable="false">
    <img src="https://www.geo.tv/assets/uploads/updates/2026-10-09/685813_4091161_updates.jpg" alt="Foreign Office Spokesperson Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan addresses weekly press briefing in Islamabad on October 9, 2026. — X@ForeignOfficePk" width="700" height="400" class="">

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="" spellcheck="false">Foreign Office Spokesperson Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan addresses weekly press briefing in Islamabad on October 9, 2026. — X@ForeignOfficePk</figcaption><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><grammarly-extension data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; position: absolute; top: 0px; left: 0px; pointer-events: none; margin: 0px; border: 0px; z-index: 1; --rem: 16;"></grammarly-extension><superhuman-go-underlines data-grammarly-shadow-root="true" class="dnXmp" style="visibility: visible !important; display: contents; --rem: 16;"></superhuman-go-underlines></figure></div><ul><li><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Pakistan to defend Saudi territory, not attack Yemen: FO.</span></li><li><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Says Islamabad continues mediation efforts between US, Iran.</span></li><li><span style="font-weight: bold; color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Afghan Taliban disagreement prevents joint statement on terrorism.<br></span></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>Pakistan on Friday reiterated its commitment to safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security, while dismissing reports that Pakistani fighter jets had taken part in cross-border operations targeting Houthi forces in Yemen.</p><p>During a weekly press briefing, Foreign Office Spokesperson Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan said that the Makkah alliance is a defensive arrangement aimed at protecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of its member countries and strengthening their collective deterrence capabilities.</p><style>

	     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});

	</div><p>Referring to the emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement held in Riyadh on October 5, he said Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye had agreed to move towards the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments.</p><p>Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif and Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir represented Pakistan in the meeting, he added.</p><p>The spokesperson said the committee reviewed the security situation and threats facing Saudi Arabia and condemned attempts to target Makkah and Madinah, as well as attacks on cities, civilians and economic infrastructure.</p><p>Khan said the three countries had approved measures to enhance readiness, military integration and their collective capacity to address security threats.</p><p>Clarifying the nature of the alliance, he said it was intended to defend member countries against aggression and that Pakistani forces would not cross into Yemen to launch attacks against Houthi forces. However, he said they could be utilised to defend Saudi territory and safeguard its sovereignty.</p><p>He said Pakistan had a substantial number of forces and resources in Saudi Arabia, adding that the alliance would assess threat perceptions and determine operational requirements in accordance with its mandate.</p><p>The spokesperson also rejected speculation about Pakistani fighter jets taking part in airstrikes against the Houthis, describing such reports as false.</p><p>Responding to questions about Pakistan’s military presence in Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson said Pakistani armed forces had been present in the Kingdom in various capacities since 1982, including under logistical arrangements and training missions.</p><p>He said further deployments would be determined according to operational requirements and decisions by the alliance’s headquarters.</p><p>He said Pakistan remained concerned about the escalation in the region, particularly because approximately 2.5 million Pakistanis resided in Saudi Arabia. He noted that the security situation could put Pakistani nationals at risk and reiterated Islamabad’s commitment to supporting their welfare.</p><p>Pakistan had consistently advocated de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy, he said, adding that the country remained committed to protecting Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">US-Iran conflict</span></h2><p>On Pakistan’s diplomatic engagement in the region, Khan said Islamabad continued to support political dialogue and efforts to reduce tensions between the United States and Iran.</p><p>He said direct communication between the two countries, including discussions on seven points, reflected the progress made through Pakistan’s mediation efforts.</p><p>The spokesperson said the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding remained in place and that Pakistan was willing to continue facilitating a negotiated solution if required.</p><p>He emphasised that diplomacy remained essential for achieving regional peace and stability, while noting that its success depended on the willingness of the parties concerned to pursue a peaceful settlement.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Terrorism emanating from Afghan territory</span></h2><p>Separately, the spokesperson said Pakistan had conveyed its concerns about terrorism emanating from Afghan territory during the eighth meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan, held in Moscow on October 5.</p><p>He said Pakistan had participated constructively in the meeting, but a joint statement was not issued because the Afghan Taliban delegation did not agree to retain previously agreed language on terrorism.</p><p>He stressed that terrorism originating from Afghanistan posed a serious security threat to neighbouring countries, particularly Pakistan, and said the absence of a joint statement should not overshadow the importance of regional dialogue.</p><p>The spokesperson also reiterated Pakistan’s position on Jammu and Kashmir, saying the dispute remained unresolved and required a settlement in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.</p><p>He welcomed the remarks of UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres during his recent visit to Pakistan regarding the role of the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP), and said its presence and role needed to be strengthened alongside efforts for a just resolution of the dispute.</p><p>The spokesperson also said Pakistan had lodged a strong protest with India following the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force personnel in the Bedian sector along the international border on October 2.</p><p>Pakistan had called for an immediate, transparent and credible investigation and appropriate action against those responsible.</p><p>He added that four injured Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25, along with the mortal remains of three Pakistani nationals, had been repatriated from Addis Ababa to Karachi on October 4, while the remaining three crew members returned on October 7, with Pakistani missions facilitating their safe return.</p>                    </div>

headline: Makkah alliance: Pakistan reaffirms support for Saudi Arabia
subheadline: Pakistani forces would not cross into Yemen to launch attacks against Houthi forces, says FO spokesperson
author: APP
article_text:
Pakistan to defend Saudi territory, not attack Yemen: FO.
Says Islamabad continues mediation efforts between US, Iran.
Afghan Taliban disagreement prevents joint statement on terrorism.

Pakistan on Friday reiterated its commitment to safeguarding Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and security, while dismissing reports that Pakistani fighter jets had taken part in cross-border operations targeting Houthi forces in Yemen.

During a weekly press briefing, Foreign Office Spokesperson Ambassador Sajjad Haider Khan said that the Makkah alliance is a defensive arrangement aimed at protecting the sovereignty and territorial integrity of its member countries and strengthening their collective deterrence capabilities.

Referring to the emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement held in Riyadh on October 5, he said Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye had agreed to move towards the practical implementation of their collective defence commitments.

Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif and Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir represented Pakistan in the meeting, he added.

The spokesperson said the committee reviewed the security situation and threats facing Saudi Arabia and condemned attempts to target Makkah and Madinah, as well as attacks on cities, civilians and economic infrastructure.

Khan said the three countries had approved measures to enhance readiness, military integration and their collective capacity to address security threats.

Clarifying the nature of the alliance, he said it was intended to defend member countries against aggression and that Pakistani forces would not cross into Yemen to launch attacks against Houthi forces. However, he said they could be utilised to defend Saudi territory and safeguard its sovereignty.

He said Pakistan had a substantial number of forces and resources in Saudi Arabia, adding that the alliance would assess threat perceptions and determine operational requirements in accordance with its mandate.

The spokesperson also rejected speculation about Pakistani fighter jets taking part in airstrikes against the Houthis, describing such reports as false.

Responding to questions about Pakistan’s military presence in Saudi Arabia, the spokesperson said Pakistani armed forces had been present in the Kingdom in various capacities since 1982, including under logistical arrangements and training missions.

He said further deployments would be determined according to operational requirements and decisions by the alliance’s headquarters.

He said Pakistan remained concerned about the escalation in the region, particularly because approximately 2.5 million Pakistanis resided in Saudi Arabia. He noted that the security situation could put Pakistani nationals at risk and reiterated Islamabad’s commitment to supporting their welfare.

Pakistan had consistently advocated de-escalation, dialogue and diplomacy, he said, adding that the country remained committed to protecting Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty.

US-Iran conflict

On Pakistan’s diplomatic engagement in the region, Khan said Islamabad continued to support political dialogue and efforts to reduce tensions between the United States and Iran.

He said direct communication between the two countries, including discussions on seven points, reflected the progress made through Pakistan’s mediation efforts.

The spokesperson said the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding remained in place and that Pakistan was willing to continue facilitating a negotiated solution if required.

He emphasised that diplomacy remained essential for achieving regional peace and stability, while noting that its success depended on the willingness of the parties concerned to pursue a peaceful settlement.

Terrorism emanating from Afghan territory

Separately, the spokesperson said Pakistan had conveyed its concerns about terrorism emanating from Afghan territory during the eighth meeting of the Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan, held in Moscow on October 5.

He said Pakistan had participated constructively in the meeting, but a joint statement was not issued because the Afghan Taliban delegation did not agree to retain previously agreed language on terrorism.

He stressed that terrorism originating from Afghanistan posed a serious security threat to neighbouring countries, particularly Pakistan, and said the absence of a joint statement should not overshadow the importance of regional dialogue.

The spokesperson also reiterated Pakistan’s position on Jammu and Kashmir, saying the dispute remained unresolved and required a settlement in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions and the aspirations of the Kashmiri people.

He welcomed the remarks of UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres during his recent visit to Pakistan regarding the role of the United Nations Military Observer Group in India and Pakistan (UNMOGIP), and said its presence and role needed to be strengthened alongside efforts for a just resolution of the dispute.

The spokesperson also said Pakistan had lodged a strong protest with India following the killing of two Pakistani civilians by Indian Border Security Force personnel in the Bedian sector along the international border on October 2.

Pakistan had called for an immediate, transparent and credible investigation and appropriate action against those responsible.

He added that four injured Pakistani crew members of MT Honour 25, along with the mortal remains of three Pakistani nationals, had been repatriated from Addis Ababa to Karachi on October 4, while the remaining three crew members returned on October 7, with Pakistani missions facilitating their safe return.

                                <div class="heading_H"><h1>Differences between PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments 'have eased'</h1></div>
                                    <div class="except" style="margin-bottom: 12px;">
                        <h2>Bilawal’s inclusion in JCP significant in the context of PPP’s reported demand for greater say in judicial appointments</h2>
                    </div>
                                <div class="time-section"  >
                                            <div class="source">
                                                            <span class="by_author">By</span>



        <div class="author_title_img" style="color:#000">
                            <a href='https://www.geo.tv/writer/ansar-abbasi'>Ansar Abbasi</a>

                        </div>
                                <span class="author_seperator"> | </span>
                            <p class="post-date-time">
                              Published October 10, 2026                            </p>
                        </div>
                                        
                </div>
            </div>
            <div class="left">
                <div class="story-area">
                    <div class="content-area">
                        <div class="medium-insert-images ui-sortable"><figure contenteditable="false">
    <img src="https://www.geo.tv/assets/uploads/updates/2026-10-10/685881_6775539_updates.jpg" alt="This representational image shows a gavel and scales of justice. — Reuters/File" width="700" height="400" class="">

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">This representational image shows a gavel and scales of justice. — Reuters/File</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b>Induction comes amid differences between two coalition partners.</b></li><li><b>Sources say differences between PPP and PML-N have eased.</b></li><li><b>Next meeting for JCP is scheduled this month on October 13.<br></b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: The induction of Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) Senator Rana Sanaullah into the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) comes amid recent differences between the two coalition partners over appointments to the superior judiciary, with sources suggesting that a fresh understanding could lead to reconsideration of PPP-backed candidates.</p><p>The two leaders were formally appointed members of the commission following the resignations of PPP Senator Farooq H Naek and PML-N member Sheikh Aftab Ahmad. Bilawal will represent the treasury benches in the National Assembly, while Rana Sanaullah will represent the Senate.</p><style>

	<script>
	     (adsbygoogle = window.adsbygoogle || []).push({});
	</script>
	</div><p>The appointments follow months of reported dissatisfaction within the PPP over its inability to secure the commission’s approval for several candidates it had supported for judicial positions.</p><p>According to media reports, Senator Farooq H Naek had proposed 33 candidates for appointments to the high courts: 16 for the Sindh High Court, 10 for the Lahore High Court, five for the Balochistan High Court and two for the Islamabad High Court. These reports said the PPP failed to secure approval for its preferred candidates in the relevant deliberations.</p><p>Sources familiar with the latest political discussions now suggest that differences between the PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments have eased. They believe the evolving understanding between the coalition partners could provide an opportunity for some PPP-backed candidates to be reconsidered in future rounds of appointments.</p><p>However, the extent of any such understanding, and whether it includes agreement on specific candidates, remains unclear. There is also no public confirmation of such an understanding by the two parties.</p><p>Bilawal’s inclusion in the commission is particularly significant in the context of the PPP’s reported demand for a greater say in judicial appointments. The party had previously expressed dissatisfaction after its preferred candidates failed to obtain the necessary support, while its senior legal representative, Farooq H Naek, had proposed candidates for several high courts. Apparently for the same reason, the Presidency had recently delayed approval of many appointments. The commission’s composition has become an important factor in the debate over judicial appointments following constitutional changes that expanded parliamentary representation in the process. Its decisions, however, continue to depend on the commission’s voting procedure.</p><p>The JCP’s next meeting is scheduled for October 13, 2026, with the extension of the term of the Sindh High Court’s constitutional benches on the reported agenda.</p><p></p>    <p class="canonical-url">

      </i>
    </p>

headline: Differences between PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments 'have eased'
subheadline: Bilawal’s inclusion in JCP significant in the context of PPP’s reported demand for greater say in judicial appointments
author: Ansar Abbasi
article_text:
Induction comes amid differences between two coalition partners.
Sources say differences between PPP and PML-N have eased.
Next meeting for JCP is scheduled this month on October 13.

ISLAMABAD: The induction of Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) Senator Rana Sanaullah into the Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) comes amid recent differences between the two coalition partners over appointments to the superior judiciary, with sources suggesting that a fresh understanding could lead to reconsideration of PPP-backed candidates.

The two leaders were formally appointed members of the commission following the resignations of PPP Senator Farooq H Naek and PML-N member Sheikh Aftab Ahmad. Bilawal will represent the treasury benches in the National Assembly, while Rana Sanaullah will represent the Senate.

The appointments follow months of reported dissatisfaction within the PPP over its inability to secure the commission’s approval for several candidates it had supported for judicial positions.

According to media reports, Senator Farooq H Naek had proposed 33 candidates for appointments to the high courts: 16 for the Sindh High Court, 10 for the Lahore High Court, five for the Balochistan High Court and two for the Islamabad High Court. These reports said the PPP failed to secure approval for its preferred candidates in the relevant deliberations.

Sources familiar with the latest political discussions now suggest that differences between the PPP and PML-N over judicial appointments have eased. They believe the evolving understanding between the coalition partners could provide an opportunity for some PPP-backed candidates to be reconsidered in future rounds of appointments.

However, the extent of any such understanding, and whether it includes agreement on specific candidates, remains unclear. There is also no public confirmation of such an understanding by the two parties.

Bilawal’s inclusion in the commission is particularly significant in the context of the PPP’s reported demand for a greater say in judicial appointments. The party had previously expressed dissatisfaction after its preferred candidates failed to obtain the necessary support, while its senior legal representative, Farooq H Naek, had proposed candidates for several high courts. Apparently for the same reason, the Presidency had recently delayed approval of many appointments. The commission’s composition has become an important factor in the debate over judicial appointments following constitutional changes that expanded parliamentary representation in the process. Its decisions, however, continue to depend on the commission’s voting procedure.

The JCP’s next meeting is scheduled for October 13, 2026, with the extension of the term of the Sindh High Court’s constitutional benches on the reported agenda.

Originally published in The News

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">People stand behind a crime scene tape. — AFP/File</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Police say victim died by suicide due to distress.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Victim's father sold plot to pay for her admission.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Police conducting autopsy to find out cause of death.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: A student of the International Islamic University Islamabad, Laiba Ijaz, allegedly died by suicide after finding out that the documents provided by an agent for admission to a US university were fake, police said on Saturday.</p><p>The victim's body was reportedly found hanging by the roadside in Islamabad’s G-10 sector, in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.</p><style>

	</div><p>According to police, the victim was distressed after discovering that the documents provided by the agent were fraudulent.</p><p>Laiba's family revealed that she had completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further studies abroad.</p><p>The family further said that an immigration consultant had demanded Rs7 million to secure her admission to a US university.</p><p>Laiba’s father, who lived with his family in a rented flat and sold milk on a motorcycle, sold his plot and paid Rs2.1 million in cash to the agent, they added.</p><p>The family said Laiba’s mother’s jewellery was also deposited with a bank to arrange the remaining amount.</p><p>They said when Laiba had the admission documents checked, she discovered that all of them were fake.</p><p>She sent a final message to her maternal uncle, saying that: “Do not tell my father about the fraud committed against me. He will die.”</p><p>Police have expanded the scope of their investigation and are examining the case from different angles.</p><p>They said they had yet to receive Laiba’s post-mortem report, adding that the actual cause of death would be determined after the report was received.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">PM Shehbaz takes notice</span></h2><p>Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken notice of the alleged suicide of Laiba, describing the incident as extremely tragic, the PM's Office said.</p><p>The premier directed the Islamabad inspector general of police and chief commissioner to immediately arrest the suspect accused of defrauding the student.</p><p>He said the suspect would be given exemplary punishment in accordance with the law.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

<h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Interior ministry orders FIA action</span></h2><p>Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the interior ministry took notice of the incident and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take immediate action.</p><p>He said the student was defrauded and authorities ordered action against those responsible.</p><p>The FIA director general was working on the case, while the FIA director had also met the victim's parents, he added. The minister said those involved in the incident would be brought to justice.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">FIA begins probe</span></h2><p>The probe agency has launched an initial inquiry into the alleged suicide of Laiba, FIA Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari said.</p><p>Describing the matter as serious, Bukhari said a case would be registered after the inquiry.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">
	<figure>
		<div class="medium-insert-embed">

		</div>
	</figure>
	<div class="medium-insert-embeds-overlay"></div>
</div>
<p>He said the suspect allegedly defrauded Laiba of Rs7.2 million on the pretext of securing her admission to a university abroad and also took Rs500,000 from her brother on the promise of arranging a job.</p><p>According to the FIA director, the suspect would pose as an employee of the Supreme Court or an officer of a government institution.</p><p>Bukhari said Laiba had planned to surprise her family on October 12 with news of her admission to Harvard University. However, two days earlier, she had the university registration certificate checked and discovered that it was fake, he added.</p><p>The FIA director also confirmed that Laiba had sent her final message to her maternal uncle.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

headline: Islamabad student allegedly dies by suicide after losing millions in US university admission scam
subheadline: PM orders Islamabad police chief, chief commissioner to arrest suspect in student fraud case
author: Ayaz Akbar Yousafzai, Azaz Syed, Duaa Mirza, Web Desk
article_text:
Police say victim died by suicide due to distress.
Victim's father sold plot to pay for her admission.
Police conducting autopsy to find out cause of death.

ISLAMABAD: A student of the International Islamic University Islamabad, Laiba Ijaz, allegedly died by suicide after finding out that the documents provided by an agent for admission to a US university were fake, police said on Saturday.

The victim's body was reportedly found hanging by the roadside in Islamabad’s G-10 sector, in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.

According to police, the victim was distressed after discovering that the documents provided by the agent were fraudulent.

Laiba's family revealed that she had completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further studies abroad.

The family further said that an immigration consultant had demanded Rs7 million to secure her admission to a US university.

Laiba’s father, who lived with his family in a rented flat and sold milk on a motorcycle, sold his plot and paid Rs2.1 million in cash to the agent, they added.

The family said Laiba’s mother’s jewellery was also deposited with a bank to arrange the remaining amount.

They said when Laiba had the admission documents checked, she discovered that all of them were fake.

She sent a final message to her maternal uncle, saying that: “Do not tell my father about the fraud committed against me. He will die.”

Police have expanded the scope of their investigation and are examining the case from different angles.

They said they had yet to receive Laiba’s post-mortem report, adding that the actual cause of death would be determined after the report was received.

PM Shehbaz takes notice

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken notice of the alleged suicide of Laiba, describing the incident as extremely tragic, the PM's Office said.

The premier directed the Islamabad inspector general of police and chief commissioner to immediately arrest the suspect accused of defrauding the student.

He said the suspect would be given exemplary punishment in accordance with the law.

Interior ministry orders FIA action

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the interior ministry took notice of the incident and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take immediate action.

He said the student was defrauded and authorities ordered action against those responsible.

The FIA director general was working on the case, while the FIA director had also met the victim's parents, he added. The minister said those involved in the incident would be brought to justice.

FIA begins probe

The probe agency has launched an initial inquiry into the alleged suicide of Laiba, FIA Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari said.

Describing the matter as serious, Bukhari said a case would be registered after the inquiry.

He said the suspect allegedly defrauded Laiba of Rs7.2 million on the pretext of securing her admission to a university abroad and also took Rs500,000 from her brother on the promise of arranging a job.

According to the FIA director, the suspect would pose as an employee of the Supreme Court or an officer of a government institution.

Bukhari said Laiba had planned to surprise her family on October 12 with news of her admission to Harvard University. However, two days earlier, she had the university registration certificate checked and discovered that it was fake, he added.

The FIA director also confirmed that Laiba had sent her final message to her maternal uncle.

article_html:
• Police say victim died by suicide due to distress.
  • Victim's father sold plot to pay for her admission.
  • Police conducting autopsy to find out cause of death.

ISLAMABAD: A student of the International Islamic University Islamabad, Laiba Ijaz, allegedly died by suicide after finding out that the documents provided by an agent for admission to a US university were fake, police said on Saturday.

The victim's body was reportedly found hanging by the roadside in Islamabad’s G-10 sector, in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.

According to police, the victim was distressed after discovering that the documents provided by the agent were fraudulent.

Laiba's family revealed that she had completed her BS degree from the International Islamic University with a gold medal and wanted to pursue further studies abroad.

The family further said that an immigration consultant had demanded Rs7 million to secure her admission to a US university.

Laiba’s father, who lived with his family in a rented flat and sold milk on a motorcycle, sold his plot and paid Rs2.1 million in cash to the agent, they added.

The family said Laiba’s mother’s jewellery was also deposited with a bank to arrange the remaining amount.

They said when Laiba had the admission documents checked, she discovered that all of them were fake.

She sent a final message to her maternal uncle, saying that: “Do not tell my father about the fraud committed against me. He will die.”

Police have expanded the scope of their investigation and are examining the case from different angles.

They said they had yet to receive Laiba’s post-mortem report, adding that the actual cause of death would be determined after the report was received.

PM Shehbaz takes notice

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has taken notice of the alleged suicide of Laiba, describing the incident as extremely tragic, the PM's Office said.

The premier directed the Islamabad inspector general of police and chief commissioner to immediately arrest the suspect accused of defrauding the student.

He said the suspect would be given exemplary punishment in accordance with the law.

Interior ministry orders FIA action

Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry said the interior ministry took notice of the incident and directed the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) to take immediate action.

He said the student was defrauded and authorities ordered action against those responsible.

The FIA director general was working on the case, while the FIA director had also met the victim's parents, he added. The minister said those involved in the incident would be brought to justice.

FIA begins probe

The probe agency has launched an initial inquiry into the alleged suicide of Laiba, FIA Director Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari said.

Describing the matter as serious, Bukhari said a case would be registered after the inquiry.

He said the suspect allegedly defrauded Laiba of Rs7.2 million on the pretext of securing her admission to a university abroad and also took Rs500,000 from her brother on the promise of arranging a job.

According to the FIA director, the suspect would pose as an employee of the Supreme Court or an officer of a government institution.

Bukhari said Laiba had planned to surprise her family on October 12 with news of her admission to Harvard University. However, two days earlier, she had the university registration certificate checked and discovered that it was fake, he added.

The FIA director also confirmed that Laiba had sent her final message to her maternal uncle.

                                <div class="heading_H"><h1>ATC disposes of Imaan, Hadi's plea against terrorism provisions in security breach case</h1></div>
                                    <div class="except" style="margin-bottom: 12px;">
                        <h2>Islamabad court proceeded with the trial in couple's absence after their defence lawyers boycott proceedings</h2>
                    </div>
                                <div class="time-section"  >
                                            <div class="source">
                                                            <span class="by_author">By</span>



        <div class="author_title_img" style="color:#000">
                            <a href='https://www.geo.tv/writer/arfa-feroz-zake'>Arfa Feroz Zake</a>

                        </div>
                                <span class="author_seperator"> | </span>
                            <p class="post-date-time">
                              Published October 10, 2026                            </p>
                        </div>
                                        
                </div>
            </div>
            <div class="left">
                <div class="story-area">
                    <div class="content-area">
                        <div class="medium-insert-images ui-sortable"><figure contenteditable="false">
    <img src="https://www.geo.tv/assets/uploads/updates/2026-10-10/685915_8999567_updates.jpg" alt="Human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari (right) with her husband and fellow lawyer Hadi Ali Chattha, during a court hearing in Islamabad on December 5, 2025. — AFP" width="700" height="400" class="">

<figcaption contenteditable="true" class="">Human rights lawyer Imaan Mazari (right) with her husband and fellow lawyer Hadi Ali Chattha, during a court hearing in Islamabad on December 5, 2025. — AFP</figcaption></figure></div><ul><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Imaan, Hadi produced before court via video link.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">ATC records three prosecution witnesses' statements.</b></li><li><b style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Judge Sipra adjourns proceedings until Monday.</b></li></ul><hr class="editorHr"><p>ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Saturday disposed of a petition challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in a security breach case registered against lawyer and human rights activist Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha.</p><p>The case, registered at Aabpara Police Station, stems from allegations that the couple posed a security risk by interfering in state affairs during the visit of an international cricket team in October 2024.</p><style>

	</div><p>The ATC in Islamabad indicted Mazari and Chattha in the case earlier this week despite the accused objecting that they had not yet received copies of the case documents.</p><p>During today's proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra questioned why the accused had not been produced before the court despite an order directing their appearance in person or through video link.</p><p>The judge directed court staff to contact Adiala jail authorities to establish why the two accused had not been brought to court. No jail official appeared before the court during the hearing.</p><p>The court subsequently sought a report from the jail authorities and briefly suspended proceedings to establish the circumstances surrounding the failure to produce the accused.</p><p>The couple was later produced via video link, where Chattha questioned why the two had not been produced before the court.</p><p>According to Chattha, they had learnt from newspaper reports the following day that charges had been framed against them in the case.</p><p>Judge Sipra responded that the accused had challenged the framing of charges, saying the high court would set aside the charge if it had not been framed correctly.</p><p>The judge also directed a jail official to submit an explanation for failing to produce Mazari and Chattha, saying the court had ordered their appearance.</p><p>The court disposed of an application challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in the case, with Judge Sipra saying the application could not be heard at the current stage of the proceedings.</p><p>The application was disposed of without hearing the defence lawyers.</p><p>Defence counsel Zainab Janjua said the accused had not been present before the court in person or via video link during the open-court proceedings.</p><p>Janjua alleged that Mazari and Chattha were being deprived of their right to a fair trial, and boycotted the proceedings along with the accused.</p><p>Following the boycott, the court proceeded with the trial in the absence of the couple and their defence lawyers, recording statements from three prosecution witnesses.</p><p>The court summoned further witnesses for Monday and adjourned the hearing until then.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Rearrest</span></h2><p>The lawyer couple has been in custody since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them over a protest outside the Islamabad High Court.</p><p>A day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case related to controversial social media posts.</p><p>On September 17, following months of proceedings, the Supreme Court suspended the couple's sentences in a case related to controversial tweets and granted them bail against surety bonds worth Rs200,000 each, until the final decision on the case pending before the Islamabad High Court.</p><p>However, the relief was short-lived. Hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court (ATC).</p><p>According to the FIR, Mazari and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads during a protest.</p>                    </div>

headline: ATC disposes of Imaan, Hadi's plea against terrorism provisions in security breach case
subheadline: Islamabad court proceeded with the trial in couple's absence after their defence lawyers boycott proceedings
author: Arfa Feroz Zake
article_text:
Imaan, Hadi produced before court via video link.
ATC records three prosecution witnesses' statements.
Judge Sipra adjourns proceedings until Monday.

ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Saturday disposed of a petition challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in a security breach case registered against lawyer and human rights activist Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha.

The case, registered at Aabpara Police Station, stems from allegations that the couple posed a security risk by interfering in state affairs during the visit of an international cricket team in October 2024.

The ATC in Islamabad indicted Mazari and Chattha in the case earlier this week despite the accused objecting that they had not yet received copies of the case documents.

During today's proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra questioned why the accused had not been produced before the court despite an order directing their appearance in person or through video link.

The judge directed court staff to contact Adiala jail authorities to establish why the two accused had not been brought to court. No jail official appeared before the court during the hearing.

The court subsequently sought a report from the jail authorities and briefly suspended proceedings to establish the circumstances surrounding the failure to produce the accused.

The couple was later produced via video link, where Chattha questioned why the two had not been produced before the court.

According to Chattha, they had learnt from newspaper reports the following day that charges had been framed against them in the case.

Judge Sipra responded that the accused had challenged the framing of charges, saying the high court would set aside the charge if it had not been framed correctly.

The judge also directed a jail official to submit an explanation for failing to produce Mazari and Chattha, saying the court had ordered their appearance.

The court disposed of an application challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in the case, with Judge Sipra saying the application could not be heard at the current stage of the proceedings.

The application was disposed of without hearing the defence lawyers.

Defence counsel Zainab Janjua said the accused had not been present before the court in person or via video link during the open-court proceedings.

Janjua alleged that Mazari and Chattha were being deprived of their right to a fair trial, and boycotted the proceedings along with the accused.

Following the boycott, the court proceeded with the trial in the absence of the couple and their defence lawyers, recording statements from three prosecution witnesses.

The court summoned further witnesses for Monday and adjourned the hearing until then.

Rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in custody since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them over a protest outside the Islamabad High Court.

article_html:
• Imaan, Hadi produced before court via video link.
  • ATC records three prosecution witnesses' statements.
  • Judge Sipra adjourns proceedings until Monday.

ISLAMABAD: An anti-terrorism court (ATC) in Islamabad on Saturday disposed of a petition challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in a security breach case registered against lawyer and human rights activist Imaan Mazari and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha.

The case, registered at Aabpara Police Station, stems from allegations that the couple posed a security risk by interfering in state affairs during the visit of an international cricket team in October 2024.

The ATC in Islamabad indicted Mazari and Chattha in the case earlier this week despite the accused objecting that they had not yet received copies of the case documents.

During today's proceedings, ATC Judge Tahir Abbas Sipra questioned why the accused had not been produced before the court despite an order directing their appearance in person or through video link.

The judge directed court staff to contact Adiala jail authorities to establish why the two accused had not been brought to court. No jail official appeared before the court during the hearing.

The court subsequently sought a report from the jail authorities and briefly suspended proceedings to establish the circumstances surrounding the failure to produce the accused.

The couple was later produced via video link, where Chattha questioned why the two had not been produced before the court.

According to Chattha, they had learnt from newspaper reports the following day that charges had been framed against them in the case.

Judge Sipra responded that the accused had challenged the framing of charges, saying the high court would set aside the charge if it had not been framed correctly.

The judge also directed a jail official to submit an explanation for failing to produce Mazari and Chattha, saying the court had ordered their appearance.

The court disposed of an application challenging the terrorism provisions invoked in the case, with Judge Sipra saying the application could not be heard at the current stage of the proceedings.

The application was disposed of without hearing the defence lawyers.

Defence counsel Zainab Janjua said the accused had not been present before the court in person or via video link during the open-court proceedings.

Janjua alleged that Mazari and Chattha were being deprived of their right to a fair trial, and boycotted the proceedings along with the accused.

Following the boycott, the court proceeded with the trial in the absence of the couple and their defence lawyers, recording statements from three prosecution witnesses.

The court summoned further witnesses for Monday and adjourned the hearing until then.

Rearrest

The lawyer couple has been in custody since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them over a protest outside the Islamabad High Court.

A day later, a sessions court sentenced them to 17 years on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) in a case related to controversial social media posts.

On September 17, following months of proceedings, the Supreme Court suspended the couple's sentences in a case related to controversial tweets and granted them bail against surety bonds worth Rs200,000 each, until the final decision on the case pending before the Islamabad High Court.

However, the relief was short-lived. Hours later, Islamabad police arrested the couple again in connection with another case and produced them before an anti-terrorism court (ATC).

According to the FIR, Mazari and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads during a protest.

<p>PPP’s Senator Sherry Rehman, Syed Naveed Qamar, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and Dr Asim Hussain were also present on the occasion.</p><p>“It was agreed in the meeting to convene separate sessions of the National Assembly and Senate on October 13,” read a statement issued by the President House.</p><div class="medium-insert-embeds" contenteditable="false">

<p>The insiders said that the federal cabinet meeting sought for 9:30am on Sunday to approve emergency in KP. </p><p>Meanwhile, PM Shehbaz telephoned Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (JUI-F) Chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman and congratulated him on performing Umrah.</p><p>The PM invited the JUI-F chief to a meeting at the Prime Minister’s House, which the latter accepted.</p><p>During the meeting, the JUI-F chief once again suggested to the premier to hold talks with PTI to end the ongoing political crisis in the country.  </p><p>He suggested resolving the issue through negotiations rather than imposing governor’s rule or an emergency in KP, the insiders added. </p><p>He reiterated his support for meaningful talks between the government and the PTI to find a way forward.</p><p>The prime minister briefed the JUI-F chief in detail on the government’s efforts to engage in dialogue with the opposition. </p><p>PM Shehbaz said the government was making every possible effort to resolve the matter through mutual understanding, sources added.</p><p>The JUI-F chief urged the prime minister to take his party’s core committee into confidence over the matter.</p><p>He has sought more time from the PM to consult the opposition and PTI on resolving the ongoing political impasse, the sources added.</p><p>The JUI-F chief, later, contacted opposition leaders and the PTI leadership in Islamabad.</p><h2><span style="color: rgb(0, 0, 0);">Federal cabinet to decide on KP emergency </span></h2><p>Speaking on <span style="font-style: italic;">Geo News</span> programme 'Naya Pakistan', KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said that no official decision has been taken on imposing an emergency or governor's rule in the province.</p><p>The governor said that said the federal cabinet would decide on Sunday whether to impose an emergency, governor's rule or both.</p><p>The governor also criticised KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, saying he should resign if he could not protect the people of his province.</p><p>Responding to a question, Kundi ruled out the possibility of further talks with the province's ruling party, the PTI. </p><p>The governor said several PTI members were either under arrest or surrendering themselves.</p><p>He alleged that the party did not want dialogue and questioned whether it could be considered a political party. Kundi further accused the PTI of engaging in talks only through confrontation and unrest.</p><h2>No room left to avoid emergency: Naqvi </h2><p>Severalty, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi said that there appears to be little room left to avoid an emergency, responding to a journalist’s question during an informal conversation with reporters.</p><p>"Is there any room left for an emergency not to be imposed?" Naqvi remarked in response to a question.</p><p>The interior minister asked them to suggest how the situation could be averted. He urged them to ask the relevant parties how many efforts he had made to find a solution.</p><p>"They themselves will tell you how far I went in my efforts to resolve the matter," Naqvi said.</p><p>The interior minister added that no room for further options remained, according to his informal remarks to journalists.</p><h2>Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi for one month </h2><p>Section 144 has been imposed across Rawalpindi district for one month, from October 10 to November 8, according to an official notification.</p><p>Under the notification, public gatherings, rallies, processions, sit-ins and protests have been banned. The gathering of five or more people is also prohibited.</p><p>The restrictions further ban carrying weapons, sticks and petrol bombs. Double riding on motorcycles and the use of loudspeakers have also been prohibited.</p><p>According to the notification, Section 144 has been enforced in view of security concerns across the district.</p><p>Legal action will be taken against those found violating the restrictions, the notification stated.</p><p>PTI-led KP government and the federal government have been odds over various issues, particularly on the counter-terrorism policy. The federal government has repeatedly asked the PTI and the provincial government in KP to shun “extremist” politics and back the Centre’s anti-terrorism policy but has failed to receive a clear, positive response.</p><p>In addition to this, the Imran Khan founded-parity, on October 4, launched a protest march towards the federal capital aimed at seeking the release of its jailed founding chairman Khan and what it describes as the restoration of constitutional supremacy.</p><p>Khan, who has been in jail since August 2023, faces multiple cases ranging from corruption to terrorism since his ouster from power via the opposition's no-trust motion in April 2022.</p><script type="module" src="https://static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js/v4bc70e2c01a94c73b74392e4234840661791215815920" integrity="sha512-L0ha0OXavK/8okipN9F8BtP84dg9DUhPERbBXzwI6dgTA55d2+yweo3pn5CSFYs45/r8md2+xvUPtTdvTNRfjA==" data-cf-beacon='{"version":"2024.11.0","token":"8291e380a9fa4889a56779ece7862f9c","spa":2}' crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
